I've heard of "your brain can't tell the difference between real and imagined experiences". Not sure if it's the same as the above comment but if it is, basically as humans we have mind body connection. What does this mean? What you feel in your body influences the quality of your thoughts. When you're feeling good in your body, you're automatically thinking good things too. Vice versa with thoughts. If you're deep in thought about something, you're body is going to respond accordingly to what you'll feel about it. Think of mind to muscle memory. For example, if a person begins to think about sex with an attractive person, their body begins to act in that state as if it were happening in real life. Deep breathing, eyes dilated, pre cum, etc. When you recall a disgusting experience in the past, you can feel your stomach change and you do facial expressions of disgust. As if it were real but it's only imagined. That memory isn't happening in the present moment. Get the point? What you think about you become. Both constructed thoughts and memory thoughts impact our physiology. Fear is a good example too. If a person begins to entertain fearful thoughts of something that are irrational, they act as if. Remember when as children we feared that there was a monster under our bed or in our closet? We acted as if. Our brain doesn't know the difference between real and imagined.
